memory_update.text: For franchise royalty/ad-fund economics, keep DPZ as the reference template but avoid over-weighting it in underfollowed discovery because it is large and high-attention.

DIN is a preferred small-cap underfollowed candidate for the node because franchise royalties and advertising revenue are a large part of franchise-segment economics, but franchisee health and legacy brand traffic must be tested.
NATH is a compact underfollowed brand-royalty/licensing candidate with restaurant and foodservice exposure; key hidden dependency is Smithfield and branded-product customer concentration.

RAVE is a speculative micro-cap exception with unusually direct disclosure to franchise royalties, advertising contributions, and supplier/distributor incentives; later layers must apply stricter liquidity, governance, and franchisee-health filters.

For this node, the core falsification path is not just consumer traffic; it is whether franchisees/licensees can absorb labor, rent, remodel, delivery, and commodity costs while still opening units, paying royalties, funding advertising, and renewing agreements.

Need next-pass search for outsourced franchise services, franchisee financing, restaurant technology vendors, ad-fund/digital demand tools, and franchise-focused REIT/real-estate dependencies rather than only brand owners.

node: Franchise royalty, advertising fund, and brand-system economics
summary: Expanded the universe around restaurant franchise royalty/ad-fund economics using a two-lane funnel. DPZ is retained only as a reference pattern for asset-light royalties plus franchisee procurement support. The underfollowed lane is more relevant for this pass: DIN and NATH fit the preferred USD 300M-10B range and have direct royalty/licensing exposure; RAVE is a below-USD-300M speculative exception because its revenue disclosure is unusually pure to franchise royalties, advertising contributions, supplier/distributor incentives, and area-development economics. Key chokepoint to test in later layers: whether franchisees/licensees can keep generating enough sales and margin after labor, rent, commodity, remodel, and delivery costs to support store openings, renewals, royalties, and advertising-fund contributions.
